cover.title: User management
p3s1i0: Use this screen to look up users registered on the platform and manage their status. It is where you create accounts and lift locks or deactivations. Only system administrators can access it. Role assignments within a project are not made here but in Permission management for each project.
p3.cap.1: User management (SCR-ACC-007) — Filtered to status “Active” and institution “Yonsei University”
p3s2i0: + Register new user — Creates an account and sends an invitation email 2.1.
p3s2i1: Search — Find users by email, name or institution. The search runs automatically a moment after you stop typing.
p3s2i2: Status filter — Five options: All · Active · Inactive · Locked · Pending invitation.
p3s2i3: Institution filter — Narrows the list by affiliated institution. Only active institutions appear in the list.
p3s2i4: ⋯ — Opens the action menu for that user 1.3.
p3s2i5: In the left menu, Platform menu > User management is the permanent entry point. You can also enter from the governance widget on the role-based dashboards.
p3s2i6: The subtitle “Platform user lookup · Status management · Invitations” describes the scope of this screen.
p3s2i7: The columns are Email · Name · Institution · Status · Last login · Created on 1.2.
p3s2i8: Status badge — Four values: Pending invitation · Active · Inactive · Locked 1.2.
p3s2i9: Email is a link — select it to go to that user's detail screen.
p3s3i0: This screen is for system administrators only. Workspace administrators do not see this item in the left menu, and if they open the URL directly, a notice about insufficient permissions is shown.
p4.title: Table columns and statuses
p4s1i0: Each row is one user. Of the six columns, Status is the one you check most often in daily work, and its value determines what you can do from the row action menu 1.3. The screenshot shows the screen with the status filter set to Active.
p4.cap.1: List table — six columns and row actions (enlarged)
p4s2i0: ⋯ — The row action menu. An open menu applies only to its own row.
p4s2i1: Email — The login account. Select it to go to the detail screen.
p4s2i3: Institution — Set from the institutions registered in Institution management.
p4s2i4: Status — Four values. Pending invitation (invitation sent only) · Active (normal) · Inactive (use suspended) · Locked (failed login attempts accumulated). An account where only the e-signature is locked gets one more badge, E-signature lock.
p4s2i5: Last login — - if the user has never logged in. This applies to users pending invitation.
p4s2i6: Created on — The date the account was created.
p4s2i7: Active badge — The screenshot has the status filter set to Active, so only this badge appears. To see what the Pending invitation badge looks like, see 2.2 and 3.2.
p4s2i8: The Email cell is a link — select it to go to that user's detail screen.
p4s3i0: Locked and inactive are different. A lock is applied automatically by the system after failed login attempts build up, so it is cleared right away by Unlock. Inactive is deliberately suspended by an administrator, so the account returns only when you Activate it.
p5.title: Row action menu
p5s1i0: Select ⋯ to show only the actions available for that user. It is normal for the number of items to differ from row to row — for example, an unlocked account has no “Unlock” item, and an account that is already active has no “Activate” item.
p5.cap.1: ⋯ menu for an active user — three items
p5.cap.2: Enlarged menu — items vary by the row's status
p5s2i0: ⋯ — Opens the menu. Select it again or select outside the menu to close it.
p5s2i1: View details — Goes to that user's detail screen. Selecting the email in the list takes you to the same place.
p5s2i2: Deactivate — Suspends the account 3.1. For your own account, the item appears dimmed with “(Not allowed for own account)” attached.
p5s2i3: Reset password — Sends a temporary password by email. Shown only for active accounts.
p5s2i4: The top row is a Pending invitation user — the menu for that row has one more item 2.2.
p5s2i5: The row whose menu is open and the other rows are all Active, so their menus have the same items. That is why there is no “Resend invitation email” item.
p5s3.name: Items added by row status
p5s3i0: Resend invitation email — Only for users pending invitation 2.2
p5s3i1: Activate — Only for inactive users (shown in place of Deactivate)
p5s3i2: Unlock — Only for accounts locked by failed logins · Runs immediately without a confirmation dialog
p5s3i3: Unlock e-signature — Only for accounts whose e-signature password is locked · Runs immediately
p5s4i0: Unlock and resending invitation emails run immediately, without a confirmation dialog. They are processed as soon as you select them, so first check that you have not selected the wrong row. There is no separate function to undo them.
p6.title: Register new user
ch2.title: User registration
sec2.1.title: Register new user
sec2.2.title: Pending invitations and resending invitation emails
p6s1i0: Creates an account and sends the invitation email at the same time. The administrator does not set a password — the user sets it directly through the invitation link sent by email. Until then, the account stays in Pending invitation status 2.2.
p6.cap.1: Register new user — no password is entered (enlarged)
p6s2i0: Email * — The login account and the address that receives the invitation email. If the address is already registered, “This email is already registered” is shown.
p6s2i2: Institution * — Select from the Active institutions registered in Institution management. If the institution you need is not listed, register it in Institution management first.
p6s2i5: Register + Send invitation — Account creation and email sending happen together. The button can be selected only when the three items marked with an asterisk are filled in.
p6s2i6: “After registration, an invitation link is sent to the email you entered. Users can log in after setting a password.” — This is why this screen has no password field.
p6s2i7: Cancel — Discards your entries and closes the dialog.
p6s2i8: Selecting outside the dialog or selecting close has the same effect.
p6s3i0: The email is the login account, so it is hard to change after registration. If there is a typo, the invitation email goes to the wrong place, and the account stays in Pending invitation status for good. Check the address once more before sending.
p7.title: Pending invitations and resending invitation emails
p7s1i0: After registration, a Pending invitation row appears at the top of the list. When the user sets a password from the invitation link, the status changes to Active. Until then, the user cannot log in. If you are contacted saying the email was not received, send it again from this row's menu.
p7.cap.1: Right after registration — a Pending invitation row appears at the top
p7.cap.2: ⋯ menu of a Pending invitation row — has one more item for resending (enlarged)
p7s2i0: ⋯ — The row action menu for a Pending invitation row.
p7s2i1: View details — Goes to that user's detail screen.
p7s2i2: Resend invitation email — Sends the invitation link again. Runs immediately without a confirmation dialog, and the label changes to “Resending…” while processing. This item is not shown for active users 1.3.
p7s2i3: Deactivate — You can also suspend an account in Pending invitation status 3.1.
p7s2i4: Reset password — For active accounts only. For users pending invitation, use Resend invitation email.
p7s2i5: The Pending invitation badge and Last login - go together — they mean the user has never logged in.
p7s2i6: Set the status filter to Pending invitation to see only users who have not yet logged in.
p7s3i0: Invitation links have an expiry period. If a user opens the link after the period has passed, the link expires. In that case, do not register the user again. Use Resend invitation email instead. Creating an account again with the same address causes a duplicate error.
p8.title: Deactivate user
ch3.title: Status management
sec3.1.title: Deactivate user
sec3.2.title: Deactivation result
p8s1i0: Suspends accounts that are no longer in use, for example due to resignation or transfer. It does not delete the account. It only blocks login, and the data and records the user left behind are kept as they are. To reverse this, select Activate in the same menu.
p8.cap.1: Deactivate user — the only one of the four actions that requires a reason (enlarged)
p8s2i0: Reason * — Required. This is recorded in the audit trail, so state the fact, such as “Resigned”. If left blank, you cannot select Run.
p8s2i1: Run — Performs the deactivation. It can be reversed, but login is blocked immediately, so check the target user before you select it.
p8s2i2: The dialog header shows the name and email of the target user. Check here that it is not someone else.
p8s2i3: “Dependent ProjectRole is released automatically (recorded in Audit Trail).” — See the precaution below.
p8s2i4: Cancel — Closes the dialog without changing anything.
p8s2i5: Selecting outside the dialog or selecting close has the same effect.
p8s3i0: When a user is deactivated, all of their project roles are released automatically. Even if you activate the user later, the roles do not come back with the account, so you must assign them again in Permission management for each project. First check whether the user has work in progress.
p9.title: Deactivation result
p9s1i0: When you finish, the dialog closes and the list reloads. The processing itself is complete, but the status badge in the list alone may not show whether the user is inactive, so the surest way to check the result is the status filter.
p9.cap.1: Right after deactivation — the badge still reads “Pending invitation”
p9s2i0: ⋯ — When you reopen the menu of a deactivated user, Activate appears in place of Deactivate. To reverse it, select that item.
p9s2i1: Status badge — Even after deactivation, it still shows Pending invitation. See the precaution below.
p9s2i2: Status filter — Set it to Inactive to see only suspended users. Check the deactivation result this way.
p9s2i3: Institution filter — When combined, it narrows the list to suspended accounts of a specific institution.
p9s3i0: If you deactivate a user who is pending invitation, the badge does not change. This is because the screen displays Pending invitation first, and the processing did not fail. To check whether the user is inactive, set the status filter to “Inactive” — a suspended account appears in that list.
